USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Systemic exposure at high doses

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient has used high-dose inhaled corticosteroids for a prolonged period and also receives a strong inhibitor of the steroid’s metabolism. The clinician reviews signs of systemic steroid excess and adrenal suppression. Which statement is most accurate?

  1. Inhaled delivery reduces but does not eliminate systemic adverse effects
  2. Inhaled drugs can never enter systemic circulation
  3. Adrenal suppression is impossible with every inhaled dose
  4. Only bronchodilators can produce systemic effects
  5. A strong metabolic inhibitor must lower steroid exposure
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Inhaled delivery reduces but does not eliminate systemic adverse effects

Systemic exposure can become clinically important with high doses and relevant interactions.

Understanding the options

Inhaled delivery reduces but does not eliminate systemic adverse effects
Systemic exposure can become clinically important with high doses and relevant interactions.
Inhaled drugs can never enter systemic circulation
Pulmonary and swallowed portions can contribute to exposure.
Adrenal suppression is impossible with every inhaled dose
High-dose and interaction-related risks exist.
Only bronchodilators can produce systemic effects
Corticosteroids can also have systemic effects.
A strong metabolic inhibitor must lower steroid exposure
Inhibition can increase exposure to a susceptible substrate.
